title: A WAY TO REDEEM WHAT WAS DEDICATED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If what they vowed is a ceremonially unclean animal - one that is not
acceptable as an offering to the LORD - the animal must be presented to
the priest, who will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the
priest then sets, that is what it will be'" - Lev 27:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Some things vowed to God could not be placed on the altar — an unclean
animal, for instance, could not be sacrificed. So God made provision. The
priest would assess its value, and the item could be redeemed, its worth
turned to use for the sanctuary.

Notice the pattern. God does not simply reject what cannot be used
directly. He provides a way for it to be valued and put to good purpose
anyway. Nothing genuinely given to God is wasted.

Dear friend, some of us feel like that unclean animal — as though what we
have to offer is not fit for God's altar. My past is too messy. My
abilities are too ordinary. My life is too broken to be of any real use.

But look at how God works. He takes what seems unusable and finds a place
for it. Paul, who had persecuted the church, became its greatest
missionary. The Samaritan woman with five failed marriages became the
first evangelist to her town (John 4:39). God specialises in redeeming
what others would discard.

Paul writes that God chose the weak things of the world to shame the
strong, and the lowly things, so that no one may boast before Him (1 Cor
1:27-29).

Bring God even the part of your life you think He cannot use. He has a way
of assigning value where you saw none.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What part of my life do I think God cannot use?
2. Do I believe God can redeem even my failures and weaknesses?
3. Where might God be assigning value I have overlooked?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that nothing given to You is wasted. Take even the
parts of my life I think are unusable, and put them to Your good purpose.
Amen.
